label: New pet at home

what_happens.title: What happens when a pet comes home
goals: The pet comes to a new home and needs time
Gentle, calm and slow is best
what_happens.parentSkill: Name the pet and its needs, and set up the pet's space together.

who_is_there.title: Who helps the pet
goals: Grown-ups are in charge of the pet
The vet helps the pet stay healthy
who_is_there.parentSkill: Make a simple family chart of pet jobs and give your child one small job.

what_i_do.title: What I do with the pet
goals: Let the pet rest and eat in peace
what_i_do.parentSkill: Show your child where and how the pet likes to be touched, and practise on a toy first.

if_scared.title: If the pet feels scary
goals: New pets can be loud, jumpy or shy
Scratches or nips can happen and can be avoided
Calm tools: stay still, step back, get a grown-up
if_scared.parentSkill: Teach the 'be a tree' move: stand still, arms folded, look at your feet, if a pet jumps.

rehearsal.title: Let's get ready for the pet
goals: Practise gentle hands on a toy
Practise calm voice and being a tree
rehearsal.parentSkill: Practise with a stuffed animal: gentle stroking, letting it "sniff" a hand, and the tree move.

steps: Get ready: a bed, bowls, food and toys for the pet
Bring the pet home in a carrier or on a lead
Let the pet explore one quiet room first
Sit calmly and let the pet come close
Gently stroke the pet the way it likes
Help with feeding, water and cleaning, with a grown-up
Wash hands after touching the pet
sensory: little paws clicking on the floor
a wet nose or a lick
honestyNotes: New pets can be shy, scared, noisy, and may scratch or nip when frightened; never promise a pet will love the child straight away or never bite. Pets need gentle hands and rest. A grown-up is responsible for the pet's care; children help. Let the parent say what kind of pet it is.

fallbackAnswer: Scared or hurt pets can nip or scratch. Gentle hands and letting it rest help a lot.
If it happens, tell a grown-up straight away.
Pets need time to get to know new people.
Being calm and gentle helps them trust you.
Maybe, with a grown-up showing you how.
Some pets like to be held, and some prefer to sit near you.
Pets bark, meow or squeak to talk.
A new home can make them noisy until they settle.
A vet is an animal doctor.
The vet helps pets stay healthy.

questionButtons.text: What can I do to help?
fallbackAnswer: You can fill the water bowl or help at feeding time.
Ask [[GROWNUP]] what job you can have.
[[GROWNUP]] will choose a cosy spot for the pet's bed.
Pets need a quiet place to rest.

questionButtons.text: Why do I wash my hands?
fallbackAnswer: Pets can carry tiny germs, so we wash hands after touching them.
It keeps everyone healthy.

questionButtons.text: Will the pet be lonely when I am at school?
fallbackAnswer: Pets rest a lot during the day.
Grown-ups make sure it has what it needs.
Some people sneeze around pet fur.
Tell [[GROWNUP]], and a doctor can help.

questionButtons.text: Can I look after it myself?
fallbackAnswer: You can do some jobs on your own as you grow.
A grown-up stays in charge and helps.

sentences.text: Soon a new pet will come to live with [[CHILD]]'s family.
It might be a puppy, a kitten, a bunny, a fish or another animal.
First [[CHILD]] helps get ready: a bed, bowls, food and toys.
Then the pet arrives in a carrier or on a lead.
Before bed, here is a story about a little girl mouse called Mila.
Mila's family was getting a pet ladybird called Dot.
First Mila helped make a leaf bed and a tiny water drop bowl.
Then Papa Mouse brought Dot home in a little box.
Dot crawled out slowly and looked around.
Mila wanted to hold her right away.
Papa said, let Dot explore first, she is new here.
Mila sat very still and very quiet.
After a while, Dot crawled onto Mila's paw.
Mila smiled the biggest smile.
Tomorrow evening, the story goes on.
Next the pet explores a quiet room, sniffing everything.
The pet may feel shy, because the home is new.
After a while, it comes closer.
Last, the family helps the pet settle in, day by day.

One day, they took Dot to the bug doctor, a gentle beetle.
Dot is healthy and happy, said the beetle.

Everyone was a pet helper.

With the new pet, [[CHILD]] uses gentle hands and a calm voice.
Stroke the pet softly, in the direction of the fur.
Some pets like their back stroked, and some do not like their tummy touched.
Let the pet come to you, instead of chasing it.
In the story, Mila the mouse learned how Dot liked to be treated.
Gentle, said Papa, use one soft finger.
Mila let Dot crawl onto her paw instead of grabbing.
Dot liked to rest on a sunny leaf after lunch.
Mila let her rest and drew her picture instead.
One day, Mila's cousin wanted to poke Dot.
Gentle, said Mila, and showed him one soft finger.
Every morning, Mila brought the water drop with Papa.
Then she washed her paws in the stream.
Dot waved her little legs, as if to say thank you.
Tomorrow evening, the story goes on.
When the pet is eating or sleeping, let it rest.
Never pull tails, ears or fur.

A new pet can feel a bit scary at first.
Puppies can jump and lick, and kittens can pounce.
Some pets bark, hiss or squeak when they feel unsure.
A pet may scratch or nip if it is scared or hurt.
In the story, Mila the mouse's cousin had a new puppy.
The puppy jumped up and licked Mila's nose.
Mila squeaked and wanted to run.
Mama did not say, he would never hurt you.
Mama said, puppies jump when they are excited, so let's be a tree.
Mila stood still, folded her arms and looked at her feet.
The puppy sniffed, then sat down.
Mila took a slow breath, like smelling a flower.
Then she held out her paw, slowly, for the puppy to sniff.
The puppy wagged its tail.
Worried and brave can happen at the same time.
Standing still like a tree helps a jumpy pet calm down.
Stepping back and calling a grown-up is always okay.
It is okay to feel unsure about a new pet.
Getting to know each other takes time.

She made a cosy leaf bed in a quiet corner.
Then she practised gentle hands on a pinecone.
One soft finger, stroke, stroke.
Papa pretended to be a jumpy puppy.
Mila stood like a tree, and they both laughed.
She practised holding her paw out slowly to sniff.
Then they talked about names, and chose Dot.
Mila said, gentle hands, calm voice, let her come to me.
She was ready.
And Mila slept well that night.

Animals feel stress in a new place, just like people, and settling can take days or weeks.
Each type of pet has different needs for food, space, exercise and rest.
Body language shows how a pet feels, like a wagging tail, flattened ears or hiding.
Learning about the pet's species before it arrives makes care easier.
[[CHILD]] can research one fact about the pet's needs.
Vets give vaccines, check teeth and help pets when they are ill, just like doctors for people.
Pet care includes daily jobs and also costs, which grown-ups plan for.
Introducing pets to each other slowly reduces fights.
Pet sitters or neighbours help when the family is away.
[[CHILD]] can take on a regular job, like brushing or feeding, with supervision.
Reading a pet's signals, like a tail swish, growl or hiss, tells you when to back off.
Most bites and scratches happen when a pet feels cornered, startled or hurt.
Handwashing matters because animals can carry germs that are harmless to them but not to people.
Training a pet with rewards works better than punishment.
[[CHILD]] can help teach the pet a simple trick, with a grown-up.
Being nervous around animals is common, and confidence grows with small, calm interactions.
Most pet fear comes from not knowing what the animal will do next; learning its body language helps.
Allergies to pets are real and a doctor can help with them.
If [[CHILD]] gets scratched or bitten, telling a grown-up straight away matters so it can be cleaned.
[[CHILD]] can set their own pace, like starting with watching, then gentle stroking.
Preparing the space, food and supplies ahead of time makes the first day calmer for the pet.
A quiet room helps a new pet decompress.
Agreeing house rules, like no pets on beds, before arrival avoids confusion.
A care schedule shared by the family keeps the pet healthy.
[[CHILD]] can make a welcome sign or a care chart.
